The College of Health Sciences Disability Services Specialist serves as the expert for the clinical programs under the College of Health Sciences: School of Medicine, School of Nursing, School of Pharmacy, and School of Population and Public Health for increasing access for and improving retention of students with permanent and temporary disabilities. Under the general direction of the Director of the Disability Services Center, the Disability Specialist will coordinate the provision of services for students enrolled in COHS programs who have a qualified disability and require access to programs and services.

This position reports to the Director of the Disability Service Center, with a dotted-line to the administration for the School of Medicine, School of Pharmacy, School of Nursing, and School of Population and Public Health. The Disability Services Specialist serves as the primary contact for prospective and newly admitted students, reviews highly sensitive and confidential disability documentation, determines reasonable accommodations, and provides ongoing disability management support. The specialist assesses and determines the nature and extent of a wide variety of disabilities, needed accommodations, and required support services, making decisions related to a wide range of accommodation issues related to the specific needs of the learners in Health Sciences.

The specialist consults with faculty and administrators in Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy, and Population and Public Health regarding student needs and disability-related curricular accommodations; interprets federal and state laws and regulations to students and faculty; facilitates projects that support the delivery of high-quality services for Health Sciences students; and coordinates with the Disability Services Center to organize and/or participate in programs to raise awareness of disability issues and empower students with disabilities to achieve academic and personal success. Decisions made by the specialist impacts university compliance and liability under federal and state disability law and regulations. The incumbent will escalate complex issues to the relevant College of Health Science administrator or campus office, as appropriate.

Because of the sensitive nature of this position, the specialist must have a deep commitment to ethical and equitable business practices and advocate for a more diverse and inclusive learning environment.
May be required to work occasional evenings/weekends.
Must have a reliable form of transportation to facilitate travel to and from requisite UCI locations.
Working knowledge of medical terminology and medical reports and their respective implications for reasonable accommodation and placement.
Advanced knowledge of the legal framework involving accommodations for students with disabilities through state and federal laws and regulations.
Strong writing, speaking, and group presentation skills in order to present information in a clear and concise manner to multiple levels in the organization in a professional manner.
Advanced knowledge of procedures for assessing and determining disability accommodations.
Demonstrated ability to exercise initiative, originality, and judgment in applying established principles to new and unusual problems.
Skill to communicate with instructors and other organizational entities regarding a student's accommodations and other academic needs.

Willingness and demonstrated ability to embrace and consistently uphold the principles of community for a collaborative work environment and communicate professionally and courteously verbally, and in written form.
Advanced knowledge of assessment, accommodation, and intervention techniques, specifically focused on meeting the unique needs of the Health Sciences' learner community.
Working knowledge of national organizations that support and further disability access in health sciences education.
Familiarity with health sciences technical standards.
